title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Public Housing Tenants’ Support) Bill 2013
portfolio: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a Housing Payment Deduction Scheme allowing compulsory deductions from specified welfare payments to cover public housing rent, arrears and required utilities.
Approved public housing lessors could request deductions after arrears exceed a prescribed minimum and reasonable recovery steps, including notice and information about support, have been taken.
The scheme would cover specified social security and student assistance payments and family tax benefit, with income-managed tenants dealt with through existing income management powers.
changes: Property damage maintenance debts would be excluded from deductible housing costs.
Requests could run for 12 months after arrears were cleared to cover ongoing rent and utilities.
Deductions would be capped by the request, available payment and applicable 35 per cent payment calculation.
Lessors would need suitable tenancy management and review processes before participating.
summary.affected: Public housing tenants receiving covered welfare payments and participating public housing lessors are affected.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: Opposed the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Public Housing Tenants' Support) Bill 2013, arguing public housing already has a 99.6 per cent rent collection rate, that its 35 per cent income deduction cap would leave a single parent with one child about $24 a day to live on, and proposed spending the bill's $8.6 million cost on services like security upgrades or solar panels for tenants instead.
